object: Square altar, 28 cm. 5 × 35 cm. including spout.
lines_described: One line of late writing round the border.
first: (1)wosi so(2)reyi (3)mlitekes?qowi te(4)liye terikelowi (5)mteron tedḫel?owi (6)ato? mẖe pso (7)a?t?[.] mẖ?e? py?ḫr
final: (1)wosi so(2)reyi (3)mlitekes?qowi te(4)liye terikelowi (5)mteron tedḫel?owi (6)ato? mẖe pso (7)a?[.] mẖ?e? p[.]ḫr
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! Malitekesh : begotten of Teliye : born of Materên. (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: At line 7 the small hatched S-shaped stroke stands just left of the long-tailed 2, as the S of a does in ato (line 6): it is the damaged left half of a, not t; the t of formula B (at mẖe) is then under the hatching.
The strokes between p and ḫ are the thin grey hatching used for damage elsewhere in this copy, not the black strokes of y; one sign's width lost (formula B: psiḫ-).

kept.why: The copy has s o r e y i with no initial a; the key allows sorey(i) for Ashêri.

unsure.why: Two strokes and a 3-shaped sign: read as q (slash + 3) then o, as in the qo that Griffith reads -qê in no 41; Griffith does not render the word.
Bold closed 3 under Griffith's ?; his Malitekesh gives sh.
Hook with a flat base under Griffith's ?; taken as the to sign of ato.
Griffith prints ? above both signs.
A faint grey tick follows o before line 7: a trace of a lost sign or of a divider; not written.
The l is hatched; read l because the word is tedḫelowi.

notes: Altar: the one line runs round the border; the copy's four rows give lines 1-3, 4, 5, 6-7 in that order, matching the rendering. Formula A here is only ato mẖe pso; formula B (line 7) breaks off after p[.]ḫr. A dot under the raised 4 (between te and liye) is not written: Griffith reads Teliye with no gap. His note on p. 592 (p636): Materên recurs in no 34 and Têlaye (sic) in no 33; found slightly displaced in front of the shrine of mastaba 2981. pp. 647-648 do not name no 36. I read pp. 647-648 during the step 2 of this text, so the step 1 readings of nos 37-41 were made knowing those notes.

object: Square altar 26 × 26 centimeters, the spout broken away.
lines_described: Border with incised line on either side, containing two lines of late writing.
first: (1)[.][.][.][.][.] (2)[.]oreyi : (3)s?p?te[.][.]l?o?wi : belilo(4)ke tmdteapeẖ?ilikr (5)terikelowi : yeteñ(6)ye : td?(7)[.][.][.][.][.][.][.] (8)ato mẖe (9) : pisoẖ?e?[.][.]k?ete?(10)se : at mlo : pisi(11)ḫrketese : ḫl(12)ẖle : ẖolk(13)[.][.][.]
final: (1)[.][.][.][.][.] (2)[.]oreyi : (3)ẖpte[.][.]l?o?wi : belilo(4)ke tmñteapesilikr (5)terikelowi : yeteñ(6)ye : tñ?(7)[.][.][.][.][.][.][.] (8)ato mẖe (9) : pisoẖ?e?[.][.]k?ete?(10)se : at mlo : pisi(11)ḫrketese : ḫl(12)ẖle : ẖolk(13)[.][.][.]
rendering: [O Wêsh! O Ash]êri! Khapate . . . : begotten of the belilêke in Tamañ Apeshilikar : of Yeteñaiye. (Formulae ABD1.)

changes.why: Griffith: Khapate; the first sign is a 3 with a tail (kh = ẖ), the second the p form.
Griffith: in Tamañ; the bold crossed sign with a blob is ñ (the ñ/d confusion).
Griffith: Apeshilikar (sh = s); the 3-shaped sign before i is s.
The crossed sign under the raised 7 has the same form as the ñ of tmñte; Griffith does not render this part.

kept.why: After ñ the copy has the y sign (three strokes) and e, with no i sign; Griffith's a is his inserted vowel, but his i stands for no sign in the copy.

unsure.could_be: a different number of lost signs
unsure.why: Five dots before the raised 2 and one dot under it; the lost sign under the 2 is the s of [s]oreyi (Griffith: Ash]êri).
A slash and an l-like sign stand inside the hatching; Griffith renders only 'Khapate . . . :'.

unsure.could_be: td; the raised 7 may mark the first dot instead
unsure.why: Not rendered by Griffith; the 7 stands over the crossed sign.
Two hatched signs (a Z-like 3 and a 9-like sign under a ?) and a hatched stretch with a long-tailed sign; the reading after piso is a guess.

unsure.where: lines 9 and 10-11, pi- of formulae A and B
unsure.why: In both formulae a 4-shaped i is joined to the p sign; Griffith's notes give pšê/pšiḫ.
Width of the final hatching estimated at about three signs.

notes: Altar border; the six rows of the copy give lines 1-13 in order, as the rendering. The two dots by the raised 13 stand at the height of the numerals and are not written. Griffith's formula notes match the copy: A ends in s (p. 647: 'an s is added at the end in nos 17, 28, 37'), B has mlê (= mlo) (p. 648), D1 'ḫlẖle : ẖêlk[...' (p. 648); the copy also ends B in se. Lines 6-7 after 'of Yeteñaiye' (': tñ? [.......]') are not rendered. Found with other slabs covering a Moslem grave against the east wall of mastaba 2981.

object: Corner broken off from an altar, showing hollowed field with part of a small deep oval trough and a circular cake in the corner.
lines_described: Remains of three lines of late inscription round the border.
rendering: Extended invocation to [Isis] and Osiris. The honourable shatamazes Mezê . . . (long gap) [: beg]otten [of . . . . .] : [kin of] the pesatê Makhes, of the pesatê N[ibelilatê] (long gap) [: malê of ma]r [?]. (Formula A . . . .)

changes.why: Griffith: shatamazes (z = d); the dotted hook is t and the looped crossed sign d.
Griffith: Mezê; the bold 3-shaped sign is m and the crossed sign d.
Griffith: [: beg]otten = [terike]lowi; S + long-tailed 2 is k + e here, not a (the a / e+k confusion).
Griffith: Makhes (m ẖ e se).
Griffith: [ma]r; the lone ν-shaped sign before the hatching is taken as the surviving half of r.

unsure.why: Two strokes and a bold 3; Griffith renders it 'The honourable'. The same group is read -qê by Griffith in no 41 (tami-tebaqê).
A slanting stroke joined to a vertical line at the left end of the row; the vertical line is taken as the break.
Dot counts as drawn: two between r and w (a third tiny dot touches r), four after t; Griffith restores Šêr[i]-wet[r]ri (p. 647). The hatched sign before i is read r.
Hatching about one and a half signs wide, with traces; expected lo.
The ν shape is the b form and the left part of se in this hand; Griffith reads r with a [?].

notes: Corner of an altar: the copy gives border lines 3, 4, 10-11, 17 and 18 (the rest lost), one row each. Extended invocation as in p. 647: '[Wêš-....]i : Šêr[i]-wet[r]ri :'. A dot under the raised 4 is not written. The vertical stroke at the left end of row 2 and the wavy line at the left end of row 3 are taken as the broken edge. Griffith: 'For the pesatê-princes, see no 44.' Found with fragments of a painted bai-statue on the north side of mastaba 1508.

object: Rectangular fragment, one end of an altar, about one third of the whole, showing an Egyptian vase with two circular hatched cakes above it, on sunk field.
lines_described: One line of late inscription round the border.

changes.why: Griffith: wakham; the 3-shaped sign with a tail to the lower left is m.

kept.why: The second sign is the open c form of ḫ, the same form the copy has in mḫe of formula B, which Griffith himself lists as mḫe for no 39 (p. 648).

unsure.why: A closed loop with a tail, unlike the c form of ḫ; read ḫ for psiḫrkete.

unsure.could_be: te + y, or a stray stroke
unsure.why: A short stroke and a dot after te taken as the divider.

notes: Altar fragment; the single border line is copied in two rows: row 1 holds lines 1-2 (right group wḫmlowi, left group ato pskete), row 2 holds line 3 (formula B). Formula A is ato pskete without mhe, as Griffith says. Found with no 38.

lines_described: Behind the head is an inscription in red ink, faint, of eight lines of late writing. The copy is from a conventionalised reading of the faded original.
first: (1)wosi : sore(2)yi : qo :? sḫi(sic)e (3)qowi ato mẖe (4)psoẖekete (5)at mẖe : p(6)sḫrkete : (7)ḫmlol : m?ol(8)kete
final: (1)wosi : sore(2)yi : qo :? sḫi(sic)e (3)qowi ato mẖe (4)psoẖekete (5)at mẖe : p(6)sḫrkete : (7)ḫmlol : ẖol(8)kete
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! The honourable(?) Shachale (?). (Formulae ABC.)

changes.why: Griffith, p. 648: formula C's second word begins with ẖêl in no 40; the 7-shaped sign with a tail is ẖ.

kept.why: The copy has the i sign, under Griffith's sic; his l is his correction of it.

unsure.why: Two strokes and a bold 3; Griffith renders it 'The honourable(?)'; the same group starts line 3 (qowi), which he does not render.

unsure.could_be: a single dot, or ? belonging to s
unsure.why: Griffith prints ? above two dots between qo and s.
Two 3-shaped signs with a slash between; read s, o, ẖ.
The raised 4 and 6 stand between two signs.

notes: Stela; the copy has two blocks: rows on the right hold lines 1-2, 3, 5-6; the shorter rows on the left, level with the second and third right rows, hold lines 3-4 and 7-8. Reading order 1-8 as the numbers. Formulae: A ato mẖe psoẖekete, B at mẖe psḫrkete, C ḫmlol : ẖolkete; p. 648 lists no 40 under C with ẖêl. Found in rubbish about grave 1519 near mastaba 2800.

object: Oblong block w. 41, h. 14 cm. sawn out of the middle of a large stele, and apparently of the full width of the stela,
lines_described: showing six lines much worn of late writing and portions of others. The lines ran somewhat obliquely.
rendering: kin of the tami-tebaqê Pashabich (?) : [kin] of the atê-mebarak . . (?) in Pakharas kar . . . (gap) : kin of the . . . (gap) : kin of the maza-qêrabar Ataqili . (?) : mar . . .

changes.why: Griffith: tami-tebaqê; the K-shaped sign with a loop is te, the ν sign b.
Griffith: Pashabich (?); the hatched signs are b and a box-shaped ḫ.
Griffith: kin of (yetmdelowi), as in lines 6 and 7; the two strokes are y and the ν-like trace at the edge of the hatching is taken as part of the lost e.
Griffith: atê-mebarak; the upright sign with a foot is b, not the barred i.
Griffith: in Pakharas (kh = ẖ); the 3 after p is ẖ.
Griffith: maza-qêrabar (z = d).
Griffith: Ataqili; the long-tailed 3 is read q with a query (it lacks the slash of q).

unsure.why: Both are hatched hooks, the first with a dot to its left (t).
A single dot stands between to and m; not written as a divider.
Hatched sign; Griffith: Pakharas.

unsure.could_be: one or two more or fewer per stretch
unsure.why: Long hatched stretches: counted at about one sign per 65 px of the enlarged pieces; lone signs inside them (n?, r?, ri?, m?, at?, o?, to?) are traces.
An S with a long stroke, then an S, before the yetmdelowi of line 6.
Griffith prints ? above this sign.
Hatched signs inside the lost stretch.

notes: Fragment of the middle of a stela; line 1 is lost and only the left end of line 2 survives (the right part of the row is blank in the copy). Rows run right to left in the order of the numbers 2-8. Griffith's rendering is a chain of 'kin of' (yetmdelowi) phrases; the qo of tami-tebaqê here is the same two-strokes-and-3 group read qo in nos 36, 38 and 40. For tami-tebaqê see no 35; found in the upper rubbish of grave 1507 at the north-east corner of the mastaba field.
